transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-01-20
Start: 14:30 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Aaron Chen (Redwood AE), Nina Rao (Redwood SE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Tom Ellis (Acme Procurement), Leila Park (Acme Legal), Marcus Ong (Acme Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Acme Sec Ops), Ravi Kapoor (Acme FinOps)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Governance checkpoint covering MSA/DPA redlines, SLA thresholds, committed pricing options and pilot scope. Action items assigned: pricing spreadsheet, DPA redline summary, private deployment runbook, pilot access.

Topics: MSA exceptions, DPA encryption/KMS, SLA uptime/latency targets, pricing tiers & commits, pilot scope and timeline, SSO/KMS integration on private deploy, data residency questions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aaron: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i think we have about an hour, we'll try to be crisp. quick roll call?
[00:07] Tom: tom here from procurement.
[00:10] Leila: leila from legal.
[00:12] Marcus: marcus, platform.
[00:14] Priya: priya, sec ops.
[00:16] Aaron: great. nina, diego with us?
[00:18] Nina: yep nina here. diego on the call as well.
[00:21] Aaron: cool. objective for today: align on the MSA/DPA asks we've seen, agree an SLA baseline for the pilot, and i'll follow up with pricing options.
[00:29] Tom: primary ask from procurement is to understand the pricing levers and what committed discounts look like. also provisioning timeline for a private pilot — we need to know when devs can hit it.
[00:40] Nina: for private we typically provide a private control plane + private runtime, can be vpc paired or on-prem. important note, there are two capacity patterns: hosted (fast onboarding) vs dedicated/reserved vs private hosted — we uh, sorry — dedicated pools which give predictable throughput.
[00:57] Marcus: clarification — we need it in our AWS accounts with our KMS and SAML SSO. is that supported?
[01:04] Nina: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping, and SAML/SSO via SSO metadata exchange. there is a small ops checklist for setting up the vpc peering and private link. i'll send the runbook.
[01:15] Priya: and audit logs? we need full audit trail to meet SOC2.
[01:19] Diego: we can stream audit events to your logging endpoint and provide configurable retention. default hosted retention is shorter but for enterprise we have extended retention add-ons.
[01:28] Leila: on the DPA side, we've flagged three items: access to raw prompts, deletion / retention windows, and subcontractor clauses. we also need indemnity language clarified.
[01:36] Aaron: noted. on deletion we offer data-at-rest encryption and configurable retention; and for hosted we can arrange data isolation. for subcontractors, our DPA includes a subprocessor list — we can provide that and discuss narrow scoping.
[01:47] Leila: ok we'll want a redline. can you provide the current DPA with the subprocessor list and a suggested redline?
[01:53] Aaron: yes. leila i'll send the DPA and a short memo calling out the three clauses you mentioned.
[01:58] Tom: pricing question — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated in terms of e2e cost? our finance team needs a predictable monthly commit number.
[02:06] Aaron: good q. roughly speaking hosted is pay-as-you-go per-token; dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity price with lower per-token compute. we typically show a committed discount when you reserve capacity for a quarter or a year. i'll put three scenarios in the spreadsheet: pilot (low commit), standard reserved (6 months), and enterprise committed (12 months) with blended unit economics.
[02:23] Ravi: can you give ballpark numbers now?
[02:26] Aaron: ballpark — depends on model family; e.g. open-style models run X, but to avoid confusion i'll send concrete numbers per model in the sheet. unfortunately different models have different quantization and perf.
[02:36] Priya: security — about KMS, is the key material ever handled by Redwood? we require customer-only key control.
[02:42] Nina: KMS integration: we do envelope encryption, the CMK resides in your account, we only see wrapped keys. we do not have plaintext key material. small caveat: for some private on-prem flows customers host the HSM.
[02:54] Priya: acceptable, we'll validate with our infosec.
[02:57] Marcus: performance SLAs — we want 95th percentile latency for < 250 tokens to be sub-200ms for the pilot. can you commit?
[03:05] Nina: for dedicated pools we have latency SLOs we've published; sub-200 at 95th is aggressive and depends on model and batch settings. in many cases with continuous batching disabled and a small batch size we can get close but i'd prefer to baseline with a short perf run.
[03:20] Marcus: ok, so baseline run as acceptance criteria for the pilot.
[03:24] Diego: yes we'll run perf tests using your prompt set, sequence length p95, and we'll provide the CSV of results.
[03:30] Leila: SLA enforcement — what remedies exist? credits? termination rights?
[03:33] Aaron: typical commercial SLA is service credits tied to monthly uptime and latency thresholds; termination for repeated failures we can discuss with legal. we'll propose a standard SLA and then you can propose edits.
[03:42] Leila: we'll likely want a cap on credits and some defined remediation timeline.
[03:46] Aaron: understood.
[03:48] Tom: procurement will need statement of work for pilot and estimated MRC for reserved capacity.
[03:53] Aaron: i'll include sample SOW language in the packet.
[03:56] Priya: data residency — our EU customers' data must stay in eu-west-1 for some workloads. can we route regionally?
[04:03] Nina: yes region pinning is supported; traffic can be routed to model endpoints in eu-west-1 and we can ensure logs and retention are region-bound. for private on-prem there are other considerations.
[04:12] Marcus: for the pilot, we want to test both hosted (fast path) and a private deployment with our KMS. is that too ambitious?
[04:19] Diego: it's doable but increases setup time. recommended path: start pilot on hosted with strict data isolation + extended retention, then bring up private runtime in parallel if pilot acceptance goes well.
[04:30] Aaron: timeline wise — if we start next week on the initial onboarding, you could be running a hosted pilot in 7-10 business days; private runtime could take 3-4 weeks depending on your infra schedule.
[04:40] Tom: good. procurement wants a target go/no-go decision after a 2-week pilot.
[04:45] Aaron: that aligns.
[04:47] Leila: the DPA redlines — is there an existing precedent with another retailer you can share?
[04:52] Nina: we have a sanitized example redline with a retailer we worked with last year; i'll include that with the DPA.
[04:57] Priya: one more on egress costs — what fees for cross-region egress if we route EU traffic to US for some models?
[05:03] Aaron: egress depends on route; we try to avoid cross-region traffic for regulated workloads. there may be transfer fees; i'll call those out in the pricing sheet as scenarios.
[05:13] Ravi: also can you clarify backup retention and deletion flows? legal may ask for proof of deletion.
[05:18] Diego: we can provide deletion API and retention config; for additional assurance we can provide a deletion report and audit trace showing key-wrapping events.
[05:28] Leila: that would help.
[05:30] Marcus: on integration, will there be an agent or is it over TLS APIs?
[05:34] Nina: it's all TLS with 1.2/1.3, mutual TLS optional for private endpoints. SDKs exist for quick dev testing.
[05:41] Tom: procurement question — will we need a PO for pilot?
[05:44] Aaron: usually pilot is covered under a pilot SOW and a small initial invoice or credit block; we'll propose options: a no-cost pilot with usage limits or a small committed pilot fee which counts toward later committed capacity.
[05:57] Tom: procurement prefers small committed fee so finance can recognize it.
[06:01] Aaron: noted. i'll include both options.
[06:04] Nina: quick note on benchmarks — to set expectations we need your prompt set and p95 sequence lengths. can marcus share a sample dataset?
[06:13] Marcus: yes i'll prepare a sanitized set and upload to the shared drive.
[06:17] Nina: perfect.
[06:19] Aaron: any competitors you're evaluating that i should be aware of?
[06:22] Tom: we're talking to openai and anthro — apologies, anthropic — and also evaluating a private model vendor.
[06:29] Aaron: ok good to know, we'll call out where we differ on private controls and cost predictability.
[06:34] Leila: one last legal question: subcontractor notifications — do you notify customers prior to onboarding new subprocessors?
[06:40] Aaron: yes we provide a subprocessor list and we notify when materially different. in the DPA we have standard notification windows.
[06:47] Leila: ok please include that.
[06:49] Aaron: wrapping up — recap of action items: i'll send pricing + SOW + DPA; nina will send runbook and sample redline; leila to send your redline; marcus to prep prompt set and VPC details; tom to confirm pilot finance approach.
[07:05] Tom: yeah procurement will confirm the committed pilot fee option by friday.
[07:09] Aaron: great. next meeting: propose a technical pilot kickoff week of 2025-02-03. we'll share calendar invite.
[07:16] Priya: one security ask — can you attest to SOC2 type II and provide last year's report?
[07:20] Diego: yes we can share our SOC2 report under NDA; i'll include instructions.
[07:25] Leila: that's it from legal. thanks.
[07:28] Aaron: thanks everyone. end.

Meeting end.
